fr.B: Car depuis des générations, Moïse est prêché dans chaque ville, et on le lit à haute voix dans les synagogues chaque sabbat. »
fr.R: En effet, depuis très longtemps, la Loi de Moïse est enseignée dans toutes les villes. Chaque jour de sabbat, on la lit à haute voix dans les synagogues. »

es.L: Porque Moisés desde generaciones antiguas tiene en cada ciudad quienes lo proclaman, siendo leído en las sinagogas cada sábado».
es.B: Porque desde hace muchas generaciones Moisés ha sido predicado en cada ciudad, y se lee en voz alta en las sinagogas cada sábado».
es.R: Porque desde hace muchísimo tiempo la ley de Moisés se enseña en todas las ciudades. Cada sábado la gente la lee en voz alta en las sinagogas».

sw.L: Kwa maana Musa tangu vizazi vya kale ana katika kila mji watu wanaomhubiri, akisomwa katika masinagogi kila Sabato."
sw.B: Kwa maana tangu vizazi vya zamani Musa amehubiriwa katika kila mji, na maandiko yake yanasomwa kwa sauti katika masinagogi kila Sabato."
sw.R: Kwa muda mrefu sana sheria ya Musa imefundishwa katika kila mji. Kila siku ya Sabato watu huisoma kwa sauti katika masinagogi."

decisions.choice: for: why these requirements are fitting
decisions.reason: "For" gives a reason, but James does not say how it connects. Most likely: Jews who know the law live in every city, so Gentile believers should respect these points for their sake. Another reading is that the law already has its teachers, and the Gentiles need not be made to keep it all.

decisions.choice: Moses: the law given through Moses, the books of Moses
decisions.reason: As in Luke 16:29 and 24:27, "Moses" stands for the writings of the law.

decisions.choice: read in the synagogues every Sabbath: the regular reading of the law
decisions.reason: The law was read and explained in the synagogue each Sabbath, as in 13:15 and 13:27.

decisions.choice: Moses has been preached; the law of Moses has been taught
alternatives: Moses has those who proclaim him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Greek around to make it clear. Readable says that "Moses" means his law, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: Τότε ἔδοξε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις σὺν ὅλῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐκλεξαμένους ἄνδρας ἐξ αὐτῶν πέμψαι εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν σὺν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ, Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν καὶ Σιλᾶν, ἄνδρας ἡγουμένους ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, γράψαντες διὰ χειρὸς αὐτῶν· Οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἀδελφοὶ τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν χαίρειν.

records.literal_gloss: Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders with all the church, having chosen men out from them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas, Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, men leading among the brothers, \v 23 having written by [the] hand of them, The apostles and the elders brothers To those in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia brothers those from among [the] Gentiles Greetings.

en.L: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send [them] to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, \v 23 having written by their hand: "The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} from among [the] Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, greetings.
en.B: Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, decided to pick men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, known as Barsabbas, and Silas, men who held leading places among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. \v 23 They sent with them this letter: "From the apostles and the elders, your brothers, to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} of Gentile birth in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: greetings.
en.R: Then the apostles and the elders and the whole church decided to choose some men from their group. They would send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, who was also called Barsabbas, and Silas. These two men were leaders among the believers. \v 23 They gave them a letter to take with them. It said: "We, the apostles and the elders, are your brothers. We are writing to you, our fellow believers who are not Jews, in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia. We send you our greetings.

fr.L: Alors il parut bon aux apôtres et aux anciens, avec toute l’église, de choisir des hommes parmi eux et [de les] envoyer à Antioche avec Paul et Barnabas : Jude appelé Barsabbas, et Silas, hommes qui avaient un rôle dirigeant parmi les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, \v 23 ayant écrit par leur main : « Les apôtres et les anciens, frères, aux {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} d’entre les nations [qui sont] à Antioche, en Syrie et en Cilicie, salut.
fr.B: Alors les apôtres et les anciens, avec toute l’église, décidèrent de choisir des hommes parmi eux et de les envoyer à Antioche avec Paul et Barnabas. Ils choisirent Jude, appelé Barsabbas, et Silas, des hommes qui occupaient une place de premier plan parmi les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. \v 23 Ils leur remirent cette lettre : « De la part des apôtres et des anciens, vos frères, aux {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} d’origine non juive qui sont à Antioche, en Syrie et en Cilicie : salut !
fr.R: Alors les apôtres, les anciens et toute l’église ont décidé de choisir quelques hommes de leur groupe. Ils les enverraient à Antioche avec Paul et Barnabas. Ils ont choisi Jude, qu’on appelait aussi Barsabbas, et Silas. Ces deux hommes étaient des responsables parmi les croyants. \v 23 Ils leur ont donné une lettre à emporter. Voici ce qu’elle disait : « Nous, les apôtres et les anciens, nous sommes vos frères. Nous vous écrivons, à vous qui partagez notre foi et qui n’êtes pas juifs, à Antioche, en Syrie et en Cilicie. Nous vous saluons.

es.L: Entonces les pareció bien a los apóstoles y a los ancianos, con toda la iglesia, escoger hombres de entre ellos y enviar[los] a Antioquía con Pablo y Bernabé: a Judas, llamado Barsabás, y a Silas, hombres principales entre los hermanos, \v 23 escribiendo por mano de ellos: «Los apóstoles y los ancianos, hermanos, a los hermanos de entre [los] gentiles que están en Antioquía, Siria y Cilicia: saludos.
es.B: Entonces los apóstoles y los ancianos, junto con toda la iglesia, decidieron escoger a algunos hombres de entre ellos y enviarlos a Antioquía con Pablo y Bernabé. Escogieron a Judas, llamado Barsabás, y a Silas, que eran dirigentes entre los hermanos. \v 23 Con ellos enviaron esta carta: «De parte de los apóstoles y los ancianos, hermanos {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}, a los hermanos de origen gentil que están en Antioquía, Siria y Cilicia: saludos.
es.R: Entonces los apóstoles, los ancianos y toda la iglesia decidieron escoger a algunos hombres de su grupo. Los enviarían a Antioquía con Pablo y Bernabé. Escogieron a Judas, al que también llamaban Barsabás, y a Silas. Estos dos hombres eran líderes entre los creyentes. \v 23 Les dieron una carta para que la llevaran. Decía así: «Nosotros, los apóstoles y los ancianos, somos hermanos {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribimos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, nuestros hermanos en la fe que no son judíos, en Antioquía, Siria y Cilicia. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} enviamos nuestros saludos.

sw.L: Ndipo ikaonekana vema kwa mitume na wazee pamoja na kanisa lote kuchagua watu miongoni mwao na kuwatuma Antiokia pamoja na Paulo na Barnaba: Yuda aitwaye Barsaba, na Sila, watu waliokuwa viongozi kati ya ndugu, \v 23 wakiwa wameandika kwa mkono wao: "Mitume na wazee, ndugu [zenu], kwa ndugu walio wa mataifa katika Antiokia na Siria na Kilikia, salamu.
sw.B: Kisha mitume na wazee, pamoja na kanisa lote, waliamua kuchagua watu miongoni mwao na kuwatuma Antiokia pamoja na Paulo na Barnaba. Waliwachagua Yuda, aitwaye Barsaba, na Sila, watu waliokuwa na nafasi za uongozi kati ya ndugu. \v 23 Waliwapa barua hii: "Kutoka kwa mitume na wazee, ndugu zenu, kwa ndugu walio wa mataifa katika Antiokia, Siria na Kilikia: Salamu.
sw.R: Ndipo mitume, viongozi wa kanisa na kanisa lote waliamua kuchagua watu fulani kati yao. Wangewatuma Antiokia pamoja na Paulo na Barnaba. Waliwachagua Yuda, aliyeitwa pia Barsaba, na Sila. Watu hao wawili walikuwa viongozi kati ya waumini. \v 23 Waliwapa barua ya kuchukua. Ilisema: "Sisi, mitume na viongozi wa kanisa, ni ndugu zenu. Tunawaandikia ninyi, waumini wenzetu msio Wayahudi, mlioko Antiokia, Siria na Kilikia. Tunawasalimu.

decisions.choice: it seemed good: they decided, as a formal resolution
decisions.reason: This is the language of official decisions, and it is repeated in the letter (15:25, 15:28).

decisions.choice: Judas Barsabbas and Silas: leaders of the Jerusalem church
decisions.reason: Silas becomes Paul's companion from 15:40, and is likely the Silvanus of Paul's letters (2 Corinthians 1:19; 1 Thessalonians 1:1; 1 Peter 5:12). Judas Barsabbas may be a relative of the Joseph Barsabbas of 1:23, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: brothers: the apostles and elders call themselves brothers of those they write to
alternatives: a third group of senders, the brothers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" stands beside "the apostles and the elders" and describes them. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "and the brothers", making the whole church senders as well. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: the city, and the Roman province around it
decisions.reason: Antioch was the chief city of Syria; Syria and Cilicia were governed together at this time. Paul had worked in this area (Galatians 1:21; Acts 9:30, 11:25-26).

decisions.choice: having written by their hand ... greetings: the letter carried by them, in the usual form of a Greek letter
decisions.reason: "By their hand" means the letter was sent with them. "Greetings" is how Greek letters began (23:26; James 1:1).

decisions.choice: From ... your brothers
alternatives: The apostles and the elders, brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the opening of the letter in the form English letters use.

decisions.choice: We, the apostles and the elders, are your brothers. We are writing to you ... We send you our greetings.
alternatives: The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the brothers ... greetings
decisions.reason: Readable turns the greeting formula into full sentences.

decisions.choice: brothers, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The senders are the apostles and elders, men, so the word is not widened. The readers, "the brothers from among the Gentiles", are believers, men and women, and take the setting.

decisions.choice: Jude appelé Barsabbas
decisions.reason: As in Acts 1:13, French usage keeps "Judas" for Judas Iscariot and calls the other men of that name "Jude". The Greek name is the same.

decisions.choice: les pareció bien (L); decidieron (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the formal phrase of a resolution; Balanced and Readable say what it means, a decision taken together (meaning decision on "it seemed good"). The same in 15:25 and 15:28.

decisions.choice: Siria, Kilikia
decisions.reason: The Roman province around Antioch (meaning decision), named "Siria" as in 14:26 and Matthew 4:24, the drafts' one name for Syria; "Kilikia" as in 6:9.

source.text: ἐπειδὴ ἠκούσαμεν ὅτι τινὲς ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξελθόντες ἐτάραξαν ὑμᾶς λόγοις ἀνασκευάζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν οἷς οὐ διεστειλάμεθα, ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν γενομένοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐκλεξαμένοις ἄνδρας πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς σὺν τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν Βαρναβᾷ καὶ Παύλῳ, ἀνθρώποις παραδεδωκόσι τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Inasmuch as we have heard that some from us having gone out troubled you by words, upsetting the minds of you, to whom not we had given instructions, \v 25 it seemed good to us having come with one accord, having chosen men to send to you with the beloved of us Barnabas and Paul, \v 26 men having handed over the lives of them for the name of the Lord of us Jesus Christ.

en.L: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your minds, to whom we gave no instructions, \v 25 it seemed good to us, having come to one mind, to choose men and send [them] to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, \v 26 men who have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: We have heard that some who went out from us have disturbed you with what they said and left you unsettled, though we gave them no such instructions. \v 25 So we have come to one mind and decided to choose men and send them to you with Barnabas and Paul, whom we love, \v 26 men who have given their lives over for the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We have heard that some people from our church came to you. We did not send them, but what they said upset you and made you worried. \v 25 So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you. They are coming with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul. \v 26 Barnabas and Paul have put their lives in danger to serve our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Puisque nous avons appris que quelques-uns, sortis de chez nous, vous ont troublés par des paroles, bouleversant vos esprits, eux à qui nous n’avions donné aucune instruction, \v 25 il nous a paru bon, étant tombés d’accord, de choisir des hommes et [de les] envoyer vers vous avec nos bien-aimés Barnabas et Paul, \v 26 des hommes qui ont livré leur vie pour le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Nous avons appris que quelques-uns, venus de chez nous, vous ont troublés par leurs discours et ont jeté le désarroi dans vos esprits, alors que nous ne leur avions donné aucune instruction de ce genre. \v 25 Nous sommes donc tombés d’accord pour choisir des hommes et vous les envoyer avec Barnabas et Paul, que nous aimons, \v 26 des hommes qui ont engagé leur vie pour le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Nous avons appris que des gens de notre église sont venus chez vous. Nous ne les avions pas envoyés, mais ce qu’ils ont dit vous a troublés et inquiétés. \v 25 Alors nous nous sommes tous mis d’accord pour choisir quelques hommes et vous les envoyer. Ils viennent avec nos chers amis Barnabas et Paul. \v 26 Barnabas et Paul ont mis leur vie en danger pour servir notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

es.L: Puesto que hemos oído que algunos que salieron de entre nosotros {{plural_you:los|os}} han inquietado con palabras, trastornando {{plural_you:las almas de ustedes|vuestras almas}}, a los cuales no dimos ninguna orden, \v 25 nos pareció bien, habiendo llegado a un mismo sentir, escoger hombres y enviar[los] a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con nuestros amados Bernabé y Pablo, \v 26 hombres que han entregado sus vidas por el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Hemos oído que algunos que salieron de entre nosotros {{plural_you:los|os}} han perturbado con lo que dijeron y {{plural_you:los|os}} han dejado confundidos, aunque nosotros no les dimos tal encargo. \v 25 Por eso, de común acuerdo, hemos decidido escoger a algunos hombres y {{plural_you:enviárselos|enviároslos}} junto con nuestros queridos Bernabé y Pablo, \v 26 que han arriesgado su vida por el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Hemos sabido que algunas personas de nuestra iglesia fueron a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}. Nosotros no los enviamos, pero lo que dijeron {{plural_you:los|os}} inquietó y {{plural_you:los|os}} dejó preocupados. \v 25 Por eso todos nos pusimos de acuerdo para escoger a algunos hombres y {{plural_you:enviárselos|enviároslos}}. Van con nuestros queridos amigos Bernabé y Pablo. \v 26 Bernabé y Pablo han puesto su vida en peligro por servir a nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa tumesikia kwamba baadhi ya waliotoka kwetu wamewasumbua kwa maneno, wakizivuruga nafsi zenu, ambao sisi hatukuwapa maagizo, \v 25 imeonekana vema kwetu, tukiwa tumekuwa na nia moja, kuchagua watu na kuwatuma kwenu pamoja na wapendwa wetu Barnaba na Paulo, \v 26 watu waliozitoa nafsi zao kwa ajili ya jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Tumesikia kwamba baadhi ya watu waliotoka kwetu wamewasumbua kwa maneno yao na kuwavuruga mioyo, ingawa sisi hatukuwapa maagizo yoyote kama hayo. \v 25 Kwa hiyo tumekubaliana kwa nia moja kuchagua watu na kuwatuma kwenu pamoja na Barnaba na Paulo tunaowapenda, \v 26 watu ambao wameyatoa maisha yao kwa ajili ya jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Tumesikia kwamba watu fulani kutoka kanisa letu walikuja kwenu. Sisi hatukuwatuma, lakini maneno yao yaliwavuruga na kuwatia wasiwasi. \v 25 Kwa hiyo sote tumekubaliana kuchagua watu fulani na kuwatuma kwenu. Wanakuja pamoja na rafiki zetu wapendwa Barnaba na Paulo. \v 26 Barnaba na Paulo wameyahatarisha maisha yao ili kumtumikia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: unsettling: turning upside down, throwing into confusion
decisions.reason: The verb was used of tearing down or packing up a house and moving out. It pictures their minds thrown into disorder.

decisions.choice: to whom we gave no instructions: the Jerusalem church did not send them
alternatives: sent them, but with other instructions
decisions.reason: The letter distances the church from the teachers of 15:1.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence goes on without saying what they taught
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "saying, You must be circumcised and keep the law"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add these words, which repeat 15:1 and 15:5. Early manuscripts do not have them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: handed over their lives: risked their lives, or gave their lives up to serve
decisions.reason: The words can mean to put one's life at risk, as Paul had at Lystra (14:19), or to give one's life over to a cause. Both fit, and both say that they had held nothing back for the Lord's name.

decisions.choice: for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: for his sake, for his cause
decisions.reason: As in 5:41 and 9:16, the name stands for the person.

decisions.choice: some people from our church; We did not send them
alternatives: some who went out from us; to whom we gave no instructions
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the church did not send the teachers, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: have put their lives in danger to serve our Lord
alternatives: have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord
decisions.reason: Readable takes the first sense in the meaning note and explains the idiom of the name.

decisions.choice: whom we love; our dear friends
decisions.reason: "Beloved" is a church word; Balanced and Readable use plain English.

decisions.choice: Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L); Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles: without the hyphen of "Jésus-Christ", so that both options read naturally; Literal follows the Greek with no article, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: qui ont engagé leur vie
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that they risked their lives or that they gave them over to serve (m4). "Engager sa vie" keeps both senses open, as the English Balanced does; "donné leur vie" would suggest that they had died.

decisions.choice: trastornando sus almas
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "almas" for the Greek word usually rendered "soul", here the inner self, the mind (meaning decision on "unsettling"); Balanced and Readable say how they were left: confused and worried.

source.text: ἀπεστάλκαμεν οὖν Ἰούδαν καὶ Σιλᾶν, καὶ αὐτοὺς διὰ λόγου ἀπαγγέλλοντας τὰ αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, and they by word [of mouth] are telling the same things.

en.L: So we have sent Judas and Silas, and they themselves will report the same things by word [of mouth].
en.B: So we are sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you the same things in person.
en.R: So we are sending Judas and Silas to you. They will tell you themselves what we have written in this letter.

fr.L: Nous avons donc envoyé Jude et Silas, qui [vous] annonceront eux aussi de vive voix les mêmes choses.
fr.B: Nous vous envoyons donc Jude et Silas, qui vous diront de vive voix la même chose.
fr.R: Nous vous envoyons donc Jude et Silas. Ils vous diront eux-mêmes ce que nous avons écrit dans cette lettre.

es.L: Hemos enviado, pues, a Judas y a Silas, y ellos mismos anunciarán de palabra lo mismo.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:les|os}} enviamos a Judas y a Silas, que {{plural_you:les|os}} dirán personalmente lo mismo.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} enviamos a Judas y a Silas. Ellos mismos {{plural_you:les|os}} dirán lo que hemos escrito en esta carta.

sw.L: Basi tumewatuma Yuda na Sila, nao wenyewe watawaeleza mambo hayo hayo kwa [mdomo].
sw.B: Kwa hiyo tunawatuma Yuda na Sila, nao watawaeleza mambo hayo hayo ana kwa ana.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tunawatuma Yuda na Sila kwenu. Wao wenyewe watawaeleza yale tuliyoandika katika barua hii.

decisions.choice: we have sent: written from the readers' point of view
decisions.reason: Letter writers often put the verb in a past tense, as the readers would see it when the letter arrived. The sense is that they are on their way with the letter.

decisions.choice: the same things: what the letter says
decisions.reason: Judas and Silas will confirm the letter by speaking, so the readers know it truly comes from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: we are sending
decisions.reason: English letters use the present here, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the Greek tense.

decisions.choice: what we have written in this letter
decisions.reason: Readable names what "the same things" are.

source.text: ἔδοξεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιτίθεσθαι ὑμῖν βάρος πλὴν τούτων τῶν ἐπάναγκες, ἀπέχεσθαι εἰδωλοθύτων καὶ αἵματος καὶ πνικτῶν καὶ πορνείας· ἐξ ὧν διατηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς εὖ πράξετε.

records.literal_gloss: It seemed good for to the Spirit the Holy and to us no further to lay upon you burden except these the necessary things, \v 29 to abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from sexual immorality; from which keeping yourselves well you will do.

en.L: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay on you no greater burden than these necessary things: \v 29 to abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well.
en.B: The Holy Spirit and we ourselves have decided to place on you no burden beyond these essentials: \v 29 keep away from food offered to idols, from blood, from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you guard yourselves against these, you will be doing what is right.
en.R: The Holy Spirit has shown us what to do, and we agree. We do not want to give you a heavy load to carry. You only need to do these few things: \v 29 Do not eat food that has been offered to idols. Do not eat blood, or meat from animals that were strangled. And do not take part in sexual sins. If you stay away from these things, you will be doing what is right.

fr.L: Car il a paru bon à l’Esprit Saint et à nous de ne vous imposer aucune autre charge que ces choses nécessaires : \v 29 vous abstenir des viandes sacrifiées aux idoles et du sang et de ce qui est étouffé et de l’immoralité sexuelle. Si vous vous gardez de ces choses, vous ferez bien.
fr.B: L’Esprit Saint et nous-mêmes avons décidé de ne vous imposer aucun fardeau en dehors de ce qui est indispensable : \v 29 gardez-vous des viandes offertes aux idoles, du sang, des animaux étouffés et de l’immoralité sexuelle. Si vous vous en gardez, vous agirez bien.
fr.R: L’Esprit Saint nous a montré ce qu’il fallait faire, et nous sommes d’accord. Nous ne voulons pas vous donner une lourde charge à porter. Vous devez seulement faire ces quelques choses : \v 29 ne mangez pas de nourriture offerte aux idoles. Ne mangez pas de sang, ni de viande d’animaux étouffés. Et ne commettez pas de péchés sexuels. Si vous évitez ces choses, vous ferez ce qui est bien.

es.L: Porque ha parecido bien al Espíritu Santo y a nosotros no {{plural_you:imponerles|imponeros}} ninguna carga más que estas cosas necesarias: \v 29 que se abstengan de lo sacrificado a los ídolos, y de sangre, y de lo estrangulado, y de inmoralidad sexual. Si {{plural_you:se guardan|os guardáis}} de estas cosas, {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} bien.
es.B: El Espíritu Santo y nosotros hemos decidido no {{plural_you:imponerles|imponeros}} ninguna carga aparte de estas cosas indispensables: \v 29 que se aparten de los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos, de la sangre, de lo estrangulado y de la inmoralidad sexual. Si {{plural_you:se guardan|os guardáis}} de estas cosas, {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} lo correcto.
es.R: El Espíritu Santo nos ha mostrado lo que debemos hacer, y nosotros estamos de acuerdo. No queremos {{plural_you:darles|daros}} una carga pesada. Solo {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} hacer estas pocas cosas: \v 29 No {{plural_you:coman|comáis}} alimentos que hayan sido ofrecidos a los ídolos. No {{plural_you:coman|comáis}} sangre ni carne de animales estrangulados. Y no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} relaciones sexuales prohibidas. Si {{plural_you:se apartan|os apartáis}} de estas cosas, {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} lo correcto.

sw.L: Kwa maana imeonekana vema kwa Roho Mtakatifu na kwetu sisi tusiwatwike mzigo wowote zaidi ya mambo haya ya lazima: \v 29 kujiepusha na vitu vilivyotolewa sadaka kwa sanamu, na damu, na [nyama ya wanyama] walionyongwa, na uasherati. Mkijilinda na mambo hayo, mtafanya vema.
sw.B: Roho Mtakatifu na sisi wenyewe tumeamua tusiwatwike mzigo wowote zaidi ya mambo haya ya lazima: \v 29 jiepusheni na vyakula vilivyotolewa kwa sanamu, na damu, na nyama ya wanyama walionyongwa, na uasherati. Mkijilinda na mambo haya, mtakuwa mnatenda yaliyo mema.
sw.R: Roho Mtakatifu ametuonyesha la kufanya, nasi tumekubali. Hatutaki kuwatwika mzigo mzito. Mnahitaji tu kufanya mambo haya machache: \v 29 Msile chakula kilichotolewa kwa sanamu. Msinywe damu, wala msile nyama ya wanyama walionyongwa. Wala msishiriki katika dhambi za zinaa. Mkijiepusha na mambo hayo, mtakuwa mnatenda yaliyo mema.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit and us: the decision is the Spirit's leading, which the church agreed with
alternatives: a human decision with a pious phrase
decisions.reason: The Spirit's guidance had been seen in the gift of the Spirit to the Gentiles (15:8) and in the Scriptures (15:15-18). The leaders claim no authority of their own apart from it (5:32, 13:2).

decisions.choice: burden: a load, here the obligations of the law
decisions.reason: The word picks up Peter's yoke of 15:10. The four requirements are all that is asked.

decisions.choice: things sacrificed to idols: meat from animals offered in pagan sacrifice
decisions.reason: The letter names plainly what James called "the pollutions of idols" (15:20). Such meat was eaten at temple feasts and sold in the market (1 Corinthians 8:1-13, 10:25-28).

decisions.choice: the order of the list: idols, blood, what is strangled, sexual immorality
decisions.reason: The letter gives the same four requirements as James did in 15:20, but puts the three about food together. Acts 21:25 has the same order.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: four requirements, with "what is strangled"
alternatives: Codex Bezae and other Western witnesses: no "what is strangled", and the added negative Golden Rule
decisions.reason: As in 15:20, the Western text drops "what is strangled" and adds a saying about not doing to others what you would not want done to yourself. Codex Bezae also adds "being carried along by the Holy Spirit" after "you will do well". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you will do well: you will be doing what is right
decisions.reason: The phrase was a common polite close in letters and can mean either "you will act rightly" or "things will go well for you". After a list of requirements, the first fits better.

decisions.choice: The Holy Spirit has shown us what to do, and we agree.
alternatives: it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us
decisions.reason: Readable explains how the Spirit and the church decided together, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: Do not eat food ...; do not eat blood, or meat from animals that were strangled
alternatives: abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled
decisions.reason: As at 15:20, Readable says what each requirement meant.

source.text: ἔρρωσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Farewell.

en.L: Farewell."
en.B: Farewell."
en.R: We wish you well. Goodbye."

fr.L: Portez-vous bien. »
fr.B: Bien à vous. »
fr.R: Nous vous souhaitons tout le bien possible. Au revoir. »

es.L: Que {{plural_you:les|os}} vaya bien».
es.B: Que {{plural_you:les|os}} vaya bien».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} deseamos lo mejor. Adiós».

sw.L: Kwaherini."
sw.B: Kwaherini."
sw.R: Tunawatakia kila la heri. Kwaherini."

decisions.choice: farewell: the usual close of a Greek letter
decisions.reason: The word means "be strong" or "stay well", and closed letters as "greetings" opened them (15:23).

decisions.choice: We wish you well. Goodbye.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the word in plain English.

decisions.choice: Portez-vous bien (L); Bien à vous (B); Nous vous souhaitons tout le bien possible. Au revoir. (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the usual close of a letter, literally a wish for good health (m1). Literal keeps that wish; Balanced uses the close of a modern French letter; "Adieu" now sounds like a parting for ever.

decisions.choice: Que les vaya bien (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Greek closing wish of a letter is a plural command, "be well" (meaning decision on farewell); Spanish says it with the third-person wish "que les vaya bien", with the plural_you setting on the pronoun.

source.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπολυθέντες κατῆλθον εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, καὶ συναγαγόντες τὸ πλῆθος ἐπέδωκαν τὴν ἐπιστολήν·

records.literal_gloss: They indeed therefore having been sent off went down to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude they delivered the letter.

en.L: So they, having been sent off, went down to Antioch, and having gathered the crowd together, they delivered the letter.
en.B: So the men were sent on their way and went down to Antioch. There they called the whole community together and handed over the letter.
en.R: So the men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. They brought all the believers together and gave them the letter.

fr.L: Eux donc, ayant pris congé, descendirent à Antioche, et ayant rassemblé la multitude, ils remirent la lettre.
fr.B: Les envoyés prirent donc congé et descendirent à Antioche. Là, ils réunirent toute la communauté et remirent la lettre.
fr.R: Les hommes ont donc quitté Jérusalem et sont allés à Antioche. Ils ont réuni tous les croyants et leur ont donné la lettre.

es.L: Ellos, pues, habiendo sido despedidos, bajaron a Antioquía, y reuniendo a la multitud, entregaron la carta.
es.B: Así que despidieron a los hombres, y estos bajaron a Antioquía. Allí reunieron a toda la comunidad y entregaron la carta.
es.R: Así que los hombres salieron de Jerusalén y fueron a Antioquía. Reunieron a todos los creyentes y les dieron la carta.

sw.L: Basi wao, wakiisha kuagwa, walishuka Antiokia, na wakiisha kuukusanya umati, waliwapa ile barua.
sw.B: Basi watu hao waliagwa, wakashuka Antiokia. Huko waliikusanya jumuiya yote ya waumini, wakawapa ile barua.
sw.R: Basi watu hao waliondoka Yerusalemu, wakaenda Antiokia. Wakawakusanya waumini wote pamoja, wakawapa ile barua.

decisions.choice: the crowd: the whole body of believers at Antioch
decisions.reason: As at 15:12 and 6:2, the word means the whole church.

decisions.choice: they: Judas and Silas, with Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: All four were sent to Antioch (15:22, 15:25).

decisions.choice: the men; left Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name those sent and the place they left.

source.text: ἀναγνόντες δὲ ἐχάρησαν ἐπὶ τῇ παρακλήσει.

records.literal_gloss: Having read [it] now they rejoiced at the encouragement.

en.L: And when they had read [it], they rejoiced at the encouragement.
en.B: When they had read it, they were glad for the encouragement it brought.
en.R: When the believers read the letter, they were very happy because it encouraged them.

fr.L: Et l’ayant lue, ils se réjouirent de l’encouragement.
fr.B: Après l’avoir lue, ils se réjouirent de l’encouragement qu’elle leur apportait.
fr.R: Quand les croyants ont lu la lettre, ils ont été très heureux, parce qu’elle les encourageait.

es.L: Y habiéndola leído, se alegraron por el consuelo.
es.B: Cuando la leyeron, se alegraron por el ánimo que les daba.
es.R: Cuando los creyentes leyeron la carta, se pusieron muy contentos, porque los animó.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kuisoma, walifurahi kwa ajili ya faraja [yake].
sw.B: Walipoisoma, walifurahi kwa sababu ya faraja iliyowaletea.
sw.R: Waumini walipoisoma barua hiyo, walifurahi sana kwa sababu iliwatia moyo.

decisions.choice: encouragement: the comfort and strength the letter gave
decisions.reason: The word can mean an appeal or a comfort. The letter freed the Gentile believers from circumcision and the whole law, so its effect was encouraging; the same word is used of Judas and Silas in 15:32.

decisions.choice: the believers read the letter
decisions.reason: Readable names who read and what.

decisions.choice: consuelo (L); el ánimo (B); los animó (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word joins comfort and encouragement (meaning decision on encouragement); Literal uses "consuelo", Balanced and Readable the everyday "ánimo", "animar".

source.text: Ἰούδας τε καὶ Σιλᾶς, καὶ αὐτοὶ προφῆται ὄντες, διὰ λόγου πολλοῦ παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐπεστήριξαν·

records.literal_gloss: Judas both and Silas also themselves prophets being, by talk much exhorted the brothers and strengthened [them].

en.L: And Judas and Silas, being prophets themselves, encouraged the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} with many words and strengthened [them].
en.B: Judas and Silas, who were also prophets, spoke at length to encourage the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and to make them strong.
en.R: Judas and Silas were prophets too. They talked with the believers for a long time and gave them courage and made their faith stronger.

fr.L: Et Jude et Silas, étant eux aussi prophètes, encouragèrent les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} par beaucoup de paroles et [les] affermirent.
fr.B: Jude et Silas, qui étaient eux aussi prophètes, parlèrent longuement pour encourager les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et les rendre forts.
fr.R: Jude et Silas étaient prophètes eux aussi. Ils ont parlé longtemps avec les croyants. Ils leur ont redonné courage et ont rendu leur foi plus forte.

es.L: Y Judas y Silas, siendo también ellos profetas, animaron a los hermanos con mucha palabra y [los] fortalecieron.
es.B: Judas y Silas, que también eran profetas, hablaron largamente para animar a los hermanos y fortalecerlos.
es.R: Judas y Silas también eran profetas. Hablaron con los creyentes durante mucho tiempo, los animaron y les ayudaron a tener una fe más fuerte.

sw.L: Na Yuda na Sila, wakiwa wao wenyewe pia manabii, waliwatia moyo ndugu kwa maneno mengi na kuwaimarisha.
sw.B: Yuda na Sila, ambao nao pia walikuwa manabii, walizungumza na ndugu kwa muda mrefu ili kuwatia moyo na kuwaimarisha.
sw.R: Yuda na Sila nao walikuwa manabii. Walizungumza na waumini kwa muda mrefu, wakawatia moyo na kuifanya imani yao iwe imara zaidi.

decisions.choice: prophets: people who spoke messages from God to the church
alternatives: people who only foretold the future
decisions.reason: Prophets in the early church spoke to build up, encourage and comfort (1 Corinthians 14:3). Prophets are named at Antioch in 11:27 and 13:1.

decisions.choice: encouraged: urged on and comforted
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the noun in 15:31 and covers both encouraging and urging.

decisions.choice: also themselves: as well as the letter, or like the prophets of Antioch
decisions.reason: "Also" may mean that they, like the letter, brought encouragement, or that they too were prophets, like those already in Antioch (13:1).

decisions.choice: made their faith stronger
decisions.reason: Readable says in what way they were strengthened, as in 14:22.

source.text: ποιήσαντες δὲ χρόνον ἀπελύθησαν μετ’ εἰρήνης ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστείλαντας αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Having continued then a time they were sent away in peace from the brothers to those having sent them.

en.L: And after they had spent some time [there], they were sent off in peace by the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} to those who had sent them.
en.B: After they had stayed there for some time, the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} let them go in peace, back to those who had sent them.
en.R: Judas and Silas stayed there for a while. Then the believers sent them back to the church in Jerusalem with a blessing of peace.

fr.L: Et après avoir passé quelque temps [là], ils furent renvoyés en paix par les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} vers ceux qui les avaient envoyés.
fr.B: Après un certain temps passé là, les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} les laissèrent repartir en paix vers ceux qui les avaient envoyés.
fr.R: Jude et Silas sont restés là quelque temps. Puis les croyants les ont renvoyés à l’église de Jérusalem en leur souhaitant la paix.

es.L: Y después de pasar [allí] algún tiempo, fueron despedidos en paz por los hermanos [para volver] a los que los habían enviado.
es.B: Después de quedarse allí algún tiempo, los hermanos los despidieron en paz para que volvieran a los que los habían enviado.
es.R: Judas y Silas se quedaron allí un tiempo. Después los creyentes los enviaron de vuelta a la iglesia de Jerusalén con una bendición de paz.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kukaa [huko] kwa muda, waliagwa kwa amani na ndugu warudi kwa wale waliokuwa wamewatuma.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kukaa huko kwa muda, ndugu waliwaaga kwa amani, wakarudi kwa wale waliokuwa wamewatuma.
sw.R: Yuda na Sila walikaa huko kwa muda. Kisha waumini waliwarudisha kwa kanisa la Yerusalemu wakiwabariki kwa amani.

decisions.choice: sent off in peace: with a farewell blessing of peace
decisions.reason: "Go in peace" was a parting blessing (16:36; Luke 7:50; 1 Corinthians 16:11).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: no verse 34
alternatives: some manuscripts add verse 34: "But it seemed good to Silas to stay there"
decisions.reason: Verse 34 is not in the SBLGNT or in the early manuscripts that it follows here, so the verse number is skipped. Some manuscripts add "But it seemed good to Silas to stay there", and Codex Bezae goes on, "and Judas went alone". The King James Version has the shorter form. The words were probably added to explain why Silas is in Antioch in 15:40, after he was sent back in this verse; but Paul could have sent for him. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Judas and Silas; the church in Jerusalem
alternatives: they; those who had sent them
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and the place, from 15:22-27.

source.text: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: Paul however and Barnabas stayed in Antioch teaching and proclaiming the good news with also others many the word of the Lord.

en.L: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming as good news, with many others also, the word of the Lord.
en.B: Paul and Barnabas, though, stayed on in Antioch. Along with many others, they taught the word of the Lord and proclaimed it as good news.
en.R: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. They and many other believers taught people the message about the Lord Jesus and told them the good news.

fr.L: Mais Paul et Barnabas séjournaient à Antioche, enseignant et annonçant comme une bonne nouvelle, avec beaucoup d’autres aussi, la parole du Seigneur.
fr.B: Paul et Barnabas, eux, restèrent à Antioche. Avec beaucoup d’autres, ils enseignaient la parole du Seigneur et l’annonçaient comme une bonne nouvelle.
fr.R: Mais Paul et Barnabas sont restés à Antioche. Avec beaucoup d’autres croyants, ils ont enseigné aux gens le message sur le Seigneur Jésus et leur ont annoncé la bonne nouvelle.

es.L: Pero Pablo y Bernabé se quedaron en Antioquía, enseñando y anunciando como buena noticia, con muchos otros también, la palabra del Señor.
es.B: Pablo y Bernabé, en cambio, se quedaron en Antioquía. Junto con muchos otros, enseñaban la palabra del Señor y la anunciaban como buena noticia.
es.R: Pero Pablo y Bernabé se quedaron en Antioquía. Ellos y muchos otros creyentes enseñaban a la gente el mensaje acerca del Señor Jesús y les anunciaban la buena noticia.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo na Barnaba walikaa Antiokia, wakifundisha na kuhubiri habari njema ya neno la Bwana, pamoja na wengine wengi pia.
sw.B: Paulo na Barnaba, kwa upande wao, walibaki Antiokia. Pamoja na wengine wengi, walifundisha neno la Bwana na kulihubiri kama habari njema.
sw.R: Lakini Paulo na Barnaba walibaki Antiokia. Wao pamoja na waumini wengine wengi waliwafundisha watu ujumbe kuhusu Bwana Yesu na kuwaambia habari njema.

decisions.choice: the word of the Lord: the message about the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 8:25 and 13:44-49, the message the apostles preached.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the good news: announcing the gospel
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the noun for gospel (15:7).

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord, following the meaning note.

source.text: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρναβᾶν Παῦλος· Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πόλιν πᾶσαν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: After now some days said to Barnabas Paul, Having turned back indeed let us look after the brothers in city every in which we have announced the word of the Lord, how they are.

en.L: And after some days Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back now and visit the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, [to see] how they are."
en.B: Some days later Paul said to Barnabas, "Come, let us go back and look in on the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every town where we announced the word of the Lord, and find out how they are doing."
en.R: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, "We should go back and visit the believers in all the towns where we told people the message about the Lord. Let us see how they are doing."

fr.L: Et après quelques jours, Paul dit à Barnabas : « Retournons donc visiter les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} dans chaque ville où nous avons annoncé la parole du Seigneur, [pour voir] comment ils vont. »
fr.B: Quelques jours plus tard, Paul dit à Barnabas : « Allons, retournons voir les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} dans toutes les villes où nous avons annoncé la parole du Seigneur, et voyons où ils en sont. »
fr.R: Quelque temps plus tard, Paul a dit à Barnabas : « Nous devrions retourner rendre visite aux croyants dans toutes les villes où nous avons annoncé le message du Seigneur. Allons voir comment ils vont. »

es.L: Y después de algunos días, Pablo dijo a Bernabé: «Volvamos ahora a visitar a los hermanos en cada ciudad en que anunciamos la palabra del Señor, [para ver] cómo están».
es.B: Algunos días después, Pablo le dijo a Bernabé: «Vamos, volvamos a visitar a los hermanos en todas las ciudades donde anunciamos la palabra del Señor, y veamos cómo les va».
es.R: Tiempo después, Pablo le dijo a Bernabé: «Debemos volver a visitar a los creyentes en todas las ciudades donde le hablamos a la gente del mensaje acerca del Señor. Vamos a ver cómo están».

sw.L: Na baada ya siku kadhaa Paulo alimwambia Barnaba, "Basi turudi sasa tukawatembelee ndugu katika kila mji ambao tulilitangaza neno la Bwana, [tuone] hali yao."
sw.B: Siku kadhaa baadaye Paulo alimwambia Barnaba, "Haya, turudi tukawatembelee ndugu katika kila mji tulimolihubiri neno la Bwana, tuone wanavyoendelea."
sw.R: Baada ya muda Paulo alimwambia Barnaba, "Turudi tukawatembelee waumini katika miji yote ambamo tuliwaambia watu ujumbe kuhusu Bwana. Tuone jinsi wanavyoendelea."

decisions.choice: visit: go to see and care for
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of God visiting in 15:14: looking after people with concern.

decisions.choice: every city where we proclaimed: the towns of the first journey
alternatives: all the cities of the empire
decisions.reason: Paul means Cyprus and the towns of southern Galatia: Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe (13:4-14:25).

decisions.choice: now: a word that gives urgency
decisions.reason: The small word adds force to the suggestion: come now, let us go.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: As at 15:1.

source.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μᾶρκον·

records.literal_gloss: Barnabas now purposed to take along also John the [one] called Mark.

en.L: And Barnabas wanted to take along also John, who was called Mark.
en.B: Barnabas wanted to bring John, also called Mark, with them too.
en.R: Barnabas wanted to take John Mark with them again.

fr.L: Et Barnabas voulait emmener aussi Jean, appelé Marc.
fr.B: Barnabas tenait à emmener avec eux Jean, surnommé Marc.
fr.R: Barnabas voulait emmener de nouveau Jean-Marc avec eux.

es.L: Y Bernabé quería llevar consigo también a Juan, el llamado Marcos.
es.B: Bernabé quería llevar también con ellos a Juan, llamado Marcos.
es.R: Bernabé quería llevar otra vez con ellos a Juan Marcos.

sw.L: Na Barnaba alitaka kumchukua pamoja nao pia Yohana aitwaye Marko.
sw.B: Barnaba alitaka wamchukue pia Yohana, aitwaye Marko, aende pamoja nao.
sw.R: Barnaba alitaka wamchukue tena Yohana Marko pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: John called Mark: Barnabas's cousin, who had begun the first journey with them
decisions.reason: His mother's house was a meeting place of the Jerusalem church (12:12). He came to Antioch with Barnabas and Saul (12:25) and set out with them as a helper (13:5). Colossians 4:10 calls him Barnabas's cousin.

decisions.choice: wanted: kept wanting, insisted
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense suggests a settled wish that Barnabas held to, set against Paul's view in 15:38.

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Readable says that Mark had gone with them before, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.

records.literal_gloss: Paul however thought fit the [one] having withdrawn from them from Pamphylia and not having gone with them to the work not to take along this [one].

en.L: But Paul thought it not right to take along this one, who had withdrawn from them from Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.
en.B: But Paul did not think it right to take with them a man who had left them in Pamphylia and had not gone on with them to the work.
en.R: But Paul did not think they should take him. On their first trip Mark had left them in Pamphylia. He did not stay with them to finish the work.

fr.L: Mais Paul jugeait bon de ne pas emmener celui-là, qui s’était éloigné d’eux depuis la Pamphylie et ne les avait pas accompagnés dans l’œuvre.
fr.B: Mais Paul estimait qu’il ne fallait pas emmener un homme qui les avait quittés en Pamphylie et ne les avait pas suivis dans l’œuvre.
fr.R: Mais Paul ne pensait pas qu’ils devaient l’emmener. Pendant leur premier voyage, Marc les avait quittés en Pamphylie. Il n’était pas resté avec eux jusqu’à la fin du travail.

es.L: Pero Pablo estimaba que no debían llevar consigo a ese, que se había apartado de ellos desde Panfilia y no había ido con ellos a la obra.
es.B: Pero Pablo no creía conveniente llevar a alguien que los había abandonado en Panfilia y no había seguido con ellos en la obra.
es.R: Pero Pablo no creía que debían llevarlo. En su primer viaje, Marcos los había dejado en Panfilia. No se quedó con ellos para terminar el trabajo.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo aliona si vema kumchukua huyu aliyejitenga nao huko Pamfilia, wala hakwenda pamoja nao kazini.
sw.B: Lakini Paulo hakuona kuwa ni vema kumchukua mtu aliyewaacha huko Pamfilia, asiendelee pamoja nao katika kazi.
sw.R: Lakini Paulo hakuona kwamba wangemchukua. Katika safari yao ya kwanza Marko aliwaacha huko Pamfilia. Hakukaa pamoja nao mpaka kazi ikamalizika.

decisions.choice: withdrew from them from Pamphylia: Mark's return to Jerusalem in 13:13
decisions.reason: At Perga in Pamphylia John left them and went back to Jerusalem (13:13). Luke does not give his reasons.

decisions.choice: withdrawn: gone away, left
decisions.reason: The verb means to go away or to fall away. In Paul's eyes Mark's leaving was a failure to stand by the work, but the word does not by itself say that he betrayed them.

decisions.choice: the work: the mission God had called them to
decisions.reason: The work for which the Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul apart (13:2, 14:26).

decisions.choice: on their first trip
decisions.reason: Readable says when this happened.

source.text: ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμὸς ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρναβᾶν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μᾶρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον, Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ τὴν Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.

records.literal_gloss: Arose therefore a sharp disagreement, so that separated they from one another, and Barnabas having taken Mark sailed to Cyprus. \v 40 Paul however having chosen Silas went forth, having been committed to the grace of the Lord by the brothers. \v 41 He was passing through then Syria and Cilicia strengthening the churches.

en.L: And there was a sharp disagreement, so that they separated from one another, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus. \v 40 But Paul chose Silas and went out, having been entrusted to the grace of the Lord by the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. \v 41 And he was going through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
en.B: The quarrel grew so heated that the two of them parted ways. Barnabas took Mark and sailed off to Cyprus, \v 40 while Paul picked Silas and set out, after the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} had commended him to the grace of the Lord. \v 41 He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches strong.
en.R: Paul and Barnabas disagreed so strongly that they split up. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed to the island of Cyprus. \v 40 Paul chose Silas to go with him. The believers prayed that the Lord would bless them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, and then Paul and Silas left. \v 41 They went through Syria and Cilicia and helped the churches there grow strong in their faith.

fr.L: Et il y eut une vive irritation, si bien qu’ils se séparèrent l’un de l’autre, et Barnabas, ayant pris Marc, s’embarqua pour Chypre. \v 40 Mais Paul choisit Silas et partit, ayant été confié à la grâce du Seigneur par les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. \v 41 Et il traversait la Syrie et la Cilicie, affermissant les églises.
fr.B: Le désaccord devint si vif qu’ils se séparèrent. Barnabas prit Marc avec lui et s’embarqua pour Chypre, \v 40 tandis que Paul choisit Silas et partit, après que les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} l’eurent confié à la grâce du Seigneur. \v 41 Il parcourut la Syrie et la Cilicie, en fortifiant les églises.
fr.R: Paul et Barnabas étaient si peu d’accord qu’ils se sont séparés. Barnabas a pris Marc avec lui et il est parti en bateau pour l’île de Chypre. \v 40 Paul a choisi Silas pour l’accompagner. Les croyants ont prié pour que le Seigneur les bénisse par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, puis Paul et Silas sont partis. \v 41 Ils ont traversé la Syrie et la Cilicie et ont aidé les églises de ces régions à devenir plus fortes dans leur foi.

es.L: Y hubo un desacuerdo tan agudo que se separaron el uno del otro, y Bernabé, tomando a Marcos, navegó a Chipre; \v 40 pero Pablo, habiendo escogido a Silas, salió, encomendado por los hermanos a la gracia del Señor. \v 41 Y pasaba por Siria y Cilicia, fortaleciendo a las iglesias.
es.B: La discusión se volvió tan fuerte que se separaron. Bernabé tomó a Marcos y se embarcó rumbo a Chipre, \v 40 mientras que Pablo escogió a Silas y partió, después de que los hermanos lo encomendaron a la gracia del Señor. \v 41 Recorrió Siria y Cilicia, fortaleciendo a las iglesias.
es.R: Pablo y Bernabé no se pusieron de acuerdo, y discutieron tanto que se separaron. Bernabé llevó a Marcos con él y se fue en barco a la isla de Chipre. \v 40 Pablo escogió a Silas para que fuera con él. Los creyentes oraron para que el Señor los bendijera con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, y luego Pablo y Silas se fueron. \v 41 Recorrieron Siria y Cilicia y ayudaron a las iglesias de allí a fortalecerse en la fe.

sw.L: Basi kukatokea ubishi mkali hata wakatengana wao kwa wao, na Barnaba akamchukua Marko akasafiri baharini kwenda Kipro. \v 40 Lakini Paulo alimchagua Sila akaondoka, akiwa amekabidhiwa na ndugu kwa neema ya Bwana. \v 41 Naye akapita katika Siria na Kilikia, akiyaimarisha makanisa.
sw.B: Ugomvi ukawa mkali kiasi kwamba wawili hao walitengana. Barnaba alimchukua Marko, akasafiri kwa meli kwenda Kipro. \v 40 Naye Paulo alimchagua Sila, akaondoka baada ya ndugu kumkabidhi kwa neema ya Bwana. \v 41 Alipita katika Siria na Kilikia, akiyaimarisha makanisa.
sw.R: Paulo na Barnaba walitofautiana sana hata wakaachana. Barnaba alimchukua Marko, wakasafiri kwa meli kwenda kisiwa cha Kipro. \v 40 Paulo alimchagua Sila aende pamoja naye. Waumini walimwomba Bwana awabariki kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kisha Paulo na Sila wakaondoka. \v 41 Walipita katika Siria na Kilikia, wakayasaidia makanisa ya huko yawe imara katika imani.

decisions.choice: a sharp disagreement: a heated clash, with strong feeling on both sides
decisions.reason: The word is used of being stirred up or provoked (17:16; 1 Corinthians 13:5). Luke tells of the quarrel plainly and does not say who was right. Later Paul speaks well of both men (1 Corinthians 9:6; Colossians 4:10; 2 Timothy 4:11).

decisions.choice: Cyprus: Barnabas's home island, where the first journey began
decisions.reason: Barnabas came from Cyprus (4:36), and it was their first stop in 13:4.

decisions.choice: entrusted to the grace of the Lord: sent off with prayer for the Lord's help
decisions.reason: As in 14:26, the church committed the missionaries to the Lord's care and favor for the work ahead.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "of the Lord"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "of God", as in 14:26. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he was going through: Paul, with Silas
decisions.reason: The verb is singular because Paul leads, but Silas is with him (16:1-3 names them both).

decisions.choice: the churches of Syria and Cilicia: the churches the letter was written to
decisions.reason: These are the churches addressed in 15:23, so Paul and Silas bring them the decision (16:4).

decisions.choice: The believers prayed that the Lord would bless them with his grace
alternatives: having been entrusted to the grace of the Lord by the brothers
decisions.reason: Readable says what entrusting to grace meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: They went; helped the churches there grow strong in their faith
decisions.reason: Readable names both travelers and says in what way the churches were strengthened.
